propositions: The epic-close bug screen catches all exceptions at the per-candidate and run-screen layers, degrading them to verdict C ('unrelated'), which silently converts systematic provider failures into a no-op with no signal in verdict, sidecar, or exit code.

When the LLM provider is misconfigured or unavailable, the verifier should fail the close (nonzero exit, error naming the provider, ticket stays in_progress) — consistent with the absent-provider path — instead of degrading to C and closing successfully.

LLMUnavailableError (including subclass LLMConfigError) must be re-raised from both screen_candidates._row and run_screen before the broad exception handler, so the close gate's fail-closed path catches it.
Non-provider per-candidate failures (malformed output, store read errors, non-LLMUnavailableError exceptions) continue to degrade to C per documented behavior.
The max_tokens re-clamp defect (model ceiling not re-applied when model shrinks) was fixed in commit e49e7a418a and is merged; this ticket addresses only the separate fail-open gate issue.
The --force-close escape hatch remains available and unchanged to allow deliberate close override when provider errors are acceptable to the operator.
